x: Option D is right: Prolaya Vema Reddi, Recherla Singama, Kolani Rudra and Kapaya Nayaka are all listed among the chiefs of the Musunuri-led liberation confederacy. The other sets include rulers outside it, such as Devaraya II, Ganapati Deva, Kumaragiri, Pedakomati Vema, Rajaraja Narendra and Kulottunga Chola.

Kumaragiri Reddi carved out the Rajahmundry division from the eastern conquests made by his brother-in-law and commander Kataya Vema, and placed it first under his son Anavota and then under Kataya Vema (1395).

The Reddi expulsion of the Velamas from Palnadu (APPSC G2 2019 key) is a separate episode from the Battle of Bhimavaram of 1367–68 near Orugallu. That is the Velama–Musunuri battle in which Anapota Nayaka's Recherla Velamas defeated and killed Kapaya Nayaka (option B names this battle, though it reverses the victor).

Vamana Bhatta Bana, at Pedakomati Vema Reddi's court, held the titles Sahitya Samrajya Dhurandhara and Sahitya Chudamani. Kavi Sarvabhauma was Srinatha's title, and the notes do not give Dharma Pratishthana Guru to Vamana Bhatta Bana.

All four pairs are correct. Kataya Vema defeated Harihara II, Annadevu took parts of Vengi with Velama help, Anavota halted the Kalinga Gangas on the Krishna, and Pedakomati Vema recovered lost land from Vijayanagara in 1404.

All three are correct. Firoz Shah's army was beaten at Kambhammetta (1396) by Gajarao Tippa and repulsed at Kandukuru (1398) by Machareddi, and he allied with Pedakomati against Rajamahendravaram (1417).

All four are correct. Kapilendra annexed Rajamahendravaram after Devaraya II's death. Purushottama won the throne after a struggle, refused to help Muhammad III and recovered ground from the Bahmanis. Prataparudra lost Udayagiri, Kondaveedu and Kondapalli to Krishnadevaraya (1513–1519).

All three are correct. Kapileswara took Cuttack in 1435 and pressed on the Reddis. The 1444 Draksharama inscription records the Vijayanagara commander Mallappa Odayar coming to help. After Deva Raya II's death, Kapileswara annexed Rajahmundry (1446–48).

All four pairs are correct. Pedakomati Vema Reddi wrote Saptasati Saratika (on Gatha Saptashati) and Bhava Dipika, Sivalinga Reddi of Kandukuru wrote Tatva Prakashika, and Vinukonda Vallabhamatya wrote the Telugu Kridabhiramam.
